newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania court rejects demand to dissolve oil giant.
newsitem.headline: Romania court rejects demand to dissolve oil giant.

text.p: The Romanian Court of Appeal rejected a legal bid to dissolve the state-run National Oil Company (CRP) on grounds it violated laws on monopolies, a senior company executive said on Tuesday.
"We've won. The court rejected the case and this means bad luck for General Trading and Investment (GTI)," CRP's vice-president Vifor Ionita told Reuters.

In October, a lower court upheld GTI's complaint that the CRP engaged in monopolistic practices but the oil company remained in business on a legal technicality. Tuesday's decision rejected outright the demand to annul a government decision last July to create the holding.

The battle had halted talks between the CRP and Chase Manhattan on a $200 million revolving loan needed by the company for vital crude oil imports this winter. The bank had asked the CRP to clarify its legal status.
GTI also complained the CRP had hindered its oil importing activity by blocking its access to the country's sole oil port, Constanta on the Black Sea.
A GTI statement said it would appeal the latest ruling to Romania's Supreme Court. But a CRP legal adviser said it "stands no chance against us in the Supreme Court".
Tuesday's was GTI's second legal setback in a month against the CRP, which groups 12 refineries, four transport and 41 oil distribution companies as well as an oil exploration company.
Last month, Bucharest's Chamber of Commerce also turned down a demand by the GTI to dissolve the oil giant.
Last winter, an acute shortage of hard currency curtailed Romania's oil imports. The Balkan country was forced to cut electricity supplies drastically to its main industries.
Sources in the oil sector told Reuters Chase Manhattan had last week accepted a government guarantee to unblock the loan.
Under the arrangement, crude imports would be carried out through the state-run Petrolexportimport SA, the country's main oil dealer, the source said.
Bank officials were not available for comment.
